The appellant filed Title Suit No.55 of 1993 against the respondents for declaration of title and for further declaration that the registered dead No.6007 executed by the defendant No. 1 in favour of the defendant No.2 on 17.02.1992 and registered on 23.06.1992 was forged, collusive, fraudulent and the same was not binding upon the plaintiff stating that the suit land originally belonged to the landlords of Kashimpur namely, Sarada Prossad Roy Chowdhury and others and C. S. record-of-right was duly prepared In their names. The suit land was vested in the Government and the plaintiff has been possessing the same The defendants, creating some rent receipts aria pattannama to grab the suit land of the government, claimed that they are the owners of the suit land. The defendants, in collusion with some employees of collectorate office, managed to change S.A. khatian by tempering and removing pages of volume books. During R.S. operation, the defendants, in collusion with settlement employees, managed to get their names recorded in R.S. Khatian collusively End fraudulently. On 17.11.1992, the appellant came to know further that the defendant No. I, as an executant, created the impugned kabala dated 17.02.1992 in respect of the suit land in favour of the defendant No.2 fraudulently. The plaintiff, thereafter, inquired into the matter and found that the defendants fraudulently managed to record the suit land in their names in both S.A. and R.S. Khatians and also created the impugned kabala deed in respect of the suit land though the suit land was the khas land of the government. Hence, was the suit. 

 9. Learned Attorney General, appearing for the government, produced a copy of the Dacca Gazette Extraordinary published by the authority on Wednesday, February 29, 1956. In serial No.9 and 10 of the schedule of the property acquired, the names of the rent receivers were published who were Babu Sakti Prosad Roy Chowdhury and others and Amula Prosad Roy Chowdhury and others. 

 No.3126 L.R.-27th February, 1956-Under the provision sub-section (2) of section 43 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (East Bengal Act XXVIII of 1951), read with section 46C of the said Act, the Governor is pleased to declare that Compensation Assessment-rolls in respect of such properties of the rent-receivers mentioned in the Schedule below as have been acquired under section 3 or will be deemed to be acquired under clause (3) of section 46E of that. Act, have been finally published under section 42 of the said Act on the date shown against each:- 

 Name of the rent-receivers 

 11. Upon close and careful perusal of the aforementioned gazette notification, it appears from the said gazette notification that the rent receiving interest of the land-lords was acquired by the government and it awarded compensation through finally publishing compensation assessment-roll in their names as per provision of sub-section 2 section of 43 of East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The Government declared that the rent receiving interest of the rent-receivers in respect of the properties mentained in the Schedule had been acquired. 

 12. In the case of Bangladesh Vs. Serajul Haque (11 BLC 714, this Court had the occasion to consider and clearly observed that "on a reading of section non-retain-able khas land belonging either to the rent receiver or to the tenants shall be deemed have been acquired by the Government and vested in the Government with the publication of a notification about final publication of the compensation assessment roll in the official gazette from the first day of the agricultural year next following the date of publication of such notification." 

 13. It was also a vivid observation advanced by this Court in Bangladesh Vs. Chowdhury Tanbir Ahmed Siddiky, (2 BLC AD 129) that "once notification under sub-section (2) of section 43 of the Act is published in the Official Gazette, such notification is conclusive proof of such publication and of the date thereof and section 72 of Act bars a Civil Court from entertaining any suit in respect of the preparation signing and publication of a Compensation Assessment-roll or any part thereof under Chapter V or chapter VA or in respect of any entry in or omission from such roll. 

 "25. Sub-section 1 of section 39 laid down that compensation payable to a rent receiver, a cultivating raiyat, a cultivating under-raiyat or a non-agricultural tenant, in respect of the acquisition of lands in his khash possession which he is not entitled to retain under section 20, shall be determined in accordance with the table mentioned in section 39. Sub-section 2 of section 39 then states that said that any dispute regarding classification of the lands for the purpose of sub-section 1 shall be referred to the prescribed revenue authority whose decision there-on shall be final. Section 40 deals with preliminary publication of Compensation Assessment-roll and then section 41 deals with appeal which can be presented with regard to assessment of compensation against the decision of the revenue authority. It is after all these that under section 42 the final publication of Compensation Assessment-roll is made. Section 44 then says that on the publication of a notification in the official gazette under subsection 2 of section 43 declaring that compensation mentioned in that section shall ensue, one of them, being that all the interests that are acquirable under the Act but have not acquired under Chapter-II of the Act shall "with the effect from the first day of the agricultural year nest following the date of publication of such notification in the official Gazettee, be deemed to have been acquired by the Government and vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances". 

 15. As such, in accordance with the provisions of section 3, 42, 43 and 44 of the Act, the consistent view on the point envisages that the publication of a notification in the official gazette declaring that a compensation assessment-roll had been finally published is a conclusive proof of such publication and of the date thereof. Even to there be any defect in the preparation and publication of the compensation assessment-roll that by itself shall not stand in the way of the vesting. Therefore, it germane to spell out that the entire chain of interest of rent-receivers will be eliminated after the publication of the compensation assessment roll, and the interests that are acquirable shall vest in the government. 

 16. It is to be mentioned that Babu Sakti Prosad Roy Chowdhury was the son of late Babu Sarada Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Roy Atul Prosad Roy Chowdhury Bahadur was son of late Babu Ananda Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Swapna Kumari Roy Chowdhury was wife of Abani Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Amulya Prosad Roy Chowdhury was son of Annanda Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Rai Arun Prosad Roy Chowdhury was son of late Amaika Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Amalendu Prosad. Roy Chowdhury, Arabindu Prosad Roy Chowdhury were sons of Amiya Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Tarn Bala Roy Chowdhury was wife of Babu Amula Prosad Roy Chowdhury of village Kashimpur, Dhaka. It thus transpires on the materials available on record that they were the rent receivers and their rent receiving interest was vested to the government on and from 08.01.1955. 

 17. The defendants' case is based on the fact that their predecessors took a settlement from the admitted owners Sarada Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Amulya Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Aboni Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Atul Prosad Roy Chowdhury, Amiyo Prosad Roy Chowdhury and Arun Proshad Roy Chowdhury on 10.09.1953. Since the defendants claimed that they took the settlement of the suit land from the rent receivers Sarada Prosad Roy Chowdhury and others onus was on them to prove such a story of settlement and to establish that they were raiyat under those rent receivers. Accordingly, in the context so appeared, it becomes unambiguous that in absence of proof of such settlement and delivery of possession, the right title and interest of the suit land should be said to be vested to the government after the publication of the aforesaid Gazette notification.

They could not produce any documentary evidence to substantiate their claim of settlement. In addition, there is no proof apparent on the face of the record that the government had not followed the pre-scribed procedure under sections 3, 42 or 43 of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 23. On the other hand, in the light of the gazette notification published on 29.02.1956, it has bean established that the rent receiving interest of the landlords was acquired by the government; to put another way, upon the final publication of the compensation assessment-roll in the gazette notification, the right, title, interest and possession of the admitted owner Saroda Prosad Roy Chowdhury and others had been vested with the government.
